facts: $\underset{\sim}{i}$ is the vector one unit to the right and $\underset{\sim}{j}$ is the vector one unit up.
The forms $(x,y)$, $x\underset{\sim}{i}+y\underset{\sim}{j}$ and $\begin{pmatrix}x\\y\end{pmatrix}$ all describe the same vector.
A positive first component means right and a negative one means left; a positive second component means up and a negative one means down.
The order is always across then up, so $6\underset{\sim}{j}+7\underset{\sim}{i}$ is written $\begin{pmatrix}7\\6\end{pmatrix}$.
A missing term means that component is zero, so $4\underset{\sim}{i}$ is the column $\begin{pmatrix}4\\0\end{pmatrix}$.
In three dimensions a third component uses $\underset{\sim}{k}$, giving $x\underset{\sim}{i}+y\underset{\sim}{j}+z\underset{\sim}{k}=\begin{pmatrix}x\\y\\z\end{pmatrix}$.
Printed vectors are bold, as in $\underset{\sim}{a}$, and handwritten ones carry a tilde underneath, as in $\underset{\sim}{a}$.
steps: Read the horizontal component: how far right (positive) or left (negative).
Read the vertical component: how far up (positive) or down (negative).
Write the components in that order, in the form the question asks for.

foundation.solution_text:
There is no $\underset{\sim}{j}$ term, so the vertical component is $0$.
$7\underset{\sim}{i}$
$=\begin{pmatrix}7\\0\end{pmatrix}$

The horizontal component is $0$, so there is no $\underset{\sim}{i}$ term.
$\begin{pmatrix}0\\-6\end{pmatrix}$
$=-6\underset{\sim}{j}$

From tail to tip the arrow goes $5$ units right and $2$ units up.
$\underset{\sim}{v}=\begin{pmatrix}5\\2\end{pmatrix}$

From tail to tip the arrow goes $3$ units left and $4$ units down.
$\underset{\sim}{w}=-3\underset{\sim}{i}-4\underset{\sim}{j}$

foundation.question_text:
A vector is written as the ordered pair $(-2,5)$.
Write it in component form and as a column vector.
foundation.solution_text:
The first number is the $\underset{\sim}{i}$ component and the second is the $\underset{\sim}{j}$ component.
$(-2,5)$
$=-2\underset{\sim}{i}+5\underset{\sim}{j}=\begin{pmatrix}-2\\5\end{pmatrix}$

The $\underset{\sim}{i}$ term goes on top, whichever order it is printed in.
$3\underset{\sim}{j}+8\underset{\sim}{i}$
$=8\underset{\sim}{i}+3\underset{\sim}{j}$
$=\begin{pmatrix}8\\3\end{pmatrix}$

development.question_text: Write $-\underset{\sim}{i}+6\underset{\sim}{j}-3\underset{\sim}{k}$ as a column vector and as an ordered triple.

development.solution_text:
From tail to tip the arrow goes $5$ units right and $4$ units down.
$\underset{\sim}{u}=\begin{pmatrix}5\\-4\end{pmatrix}$

development.question_text: Write $5\underset{\sim}{i}-2\underset{\sim}{k}$ as a column vector in three dimensions.
development.solution_text:
There is no $\underset{\sim}{j}$ term, so the middle component is $0$.
$5\underset{\sim}{i}-2\underset{\sim}{k}$
$=\begin{pmatrix}5\\0\\-2\end{pmatrix}$

development.question_text:
State whether $3\underset{\sim}{i}-4\underset{\sim}{j}$ and $\begin{pmatrix}-4\\3\end{pmatrix}$ are the same vector.
Give a reason.
development.solution_text:
$3\underset{\sim}{i}-4\underset{\sim}{j}$ has horizontal component $3$ and vertical component $-4$.
$\begin{pmatrix}-4\\3\end{pmatrix}$ has horizontal component $-4$ and vertical component $3$.
They are not the same vector, because the components have been swapped.

mastery.question_text: Write $-4\underset{\sim}{k}+2\underset{\sim}{i}-\underset{\sim}{j}$ as a column vector and as an ordered triple.
mastery.solution_text:
Put the terms in the order $\underset{\sim}{i}$, $\underset{\sim}{j}$, $\underset{\sim}{k}$ first.
$-4\underset{\sim}{k}+2\underset{\sim}{i}-\underset{\sim}{j}$
$=2\underset{\sim}{i}-\underset{\sim}{j}-4\underset{\sim}{k}$
$=\begin{pmatrix}2\\-1\\-4\end{pmatrix}=(2,-1,-4)$

mastery.question_text:
State whether $-3\underset{\sim}{i}+6\underset{\sim}{k}$ and the ordered triple $(-3,0,6)$ represent the same vector.
Give a reason.
mastery.solution_text:
$-3\underset{\sim}{i}+6\underset{\sim}{k}$ has no $\underset{\sim}{j}$ term, so its middle component is $0$.
$-3\underset{\sim}{i}+6\underset{\sim}{k}=(-3,0,6)$
They are the same vector, because all three components match.

mastery.question_text:
The vector $2\underset{\sim}{i}-\underset{\sim}{j}+p\underset{\sim}{k}$ is written as the column vector $\begin{pmatrix}q\\-1\\5\end{pmatrix}$.
Find $p$ and $q$.
mastery.solution_text:
Match the components row by row.
The $\underset{\sim}{i}$ component is the top entry, so $q=2$.
The $\underset{\sim}{k}$ component is the bottom entry, so $p=5$.
$p=5$ and $q=2$
